import pytest

# Assuming the function is in a module named `color_utils.py`
# from color_utils import rgb_to_hex


def test_rgb_to_hex_happy_path():
    """Test typical RGB-to-hex conversions."""
    assert rgb_to_hex(255, 0, 0) == "#ff0000"
    assert rgb_to_hex(0, 255, 0) == "#00ff00"
    assert rgb_to_hex(0, 0, 255) == "#0000ff"
    assert rgb_to_hex(255, 255, 255) == "#ffffff"
    assert rgb_to_hex(0, 0, 0) == "#000000"
    assert rgb_to_hex(128, 128, 128) == "#808080"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "r, g, b, expected",
    [
        (0, 0, 0, "#000000"),          # absolute minimum
        (255, 255, 255, "#ffffff"),    # absolute maximum
        (1, 2, 3, "#010203"),          # single-digit hex padding
        (15, 16, 17, "#0f1011"),       # two-digit boundaries
        (254, 253, 252, "#fefdfc"),    # near maximum
    ],
)
def test_rgb_to_hex_edge_cases(r, g, b, expected):
    """Test edge values for single-digit padding, min, and max."""
    assert rgb_to_hex(r, g, b) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "r, g, b",
    [
        (-1, 0, 0),
        (0, -1, 0),
        (0, 0, -1),
        (256, 0, 0),
        (0, 256, 0),
        (0, 0, 256),
        (-1, -1, -1),
        (300, 255, 255),
        (255, 300, 255),
        (255, 255, 300),
    ],
)
def test_rgb_to_hex_invalid_range_raises_value_error(r, g, b):
    """Test that values outside 0-255 raise ValueError with the expected message."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="RGB values must be 0-255"):
        rgb_to_hex(r, g, b)
